name: Payment Retry Plan
title: Retry declined card payments instead of cancelling the order

summary: Checkout cancels an order the moment the card is declined, even when the bank says "try again later". In March that cancelled **1,240 orders** that would most likely have gone through on a second try.

This plan retries soft declines on a backoff schedule, makes every charge idempotent so a retry can never charge twice, and rolls out behind a flag. Hard declines (stolen card, closed account) still cancel at once.
steps: Sort declines into soft (retry) and hard (cancel) by the gateway's decline code (chapter 2).
Schedule up to three retries for soft declines, and email the customer when the first one is scheduled (chapter 2).
Send an idempotency key with every charge and record each attempt (chapter 3).
Ship behind `payment_retry_enabled`, at 10% of orders and then 100% (chapter 4).

chapters.title: Why good orders get cancelled
explain: `checkout()` treats every decline the same way: it calls `order.cancel()` and shows "Payment failed". The gateway already says which declines are temporary, but nothing reads that code.
Most soft declines are insufficient funds on payday eve, a bank's fraud check that clears in minutes, or a gateway timeout. Customers who notice place the order again by hand. The rest are lost.

chapters.title: Retry soft declines on a backoff schedule
explain: A new `classify_decline()` reads the gateway's decline code. Hard declines cancel as today. Soft declines move the order to `retrying` and queue a `RetryWorker` job instead.
The worker charges again on a fixed schedule. A success marks the order paid as usual. After the last failed retry it cancels the order and sends today's "Payment failed" email.

chapters.title: Make every charge idempotent
explain: `charge()` will send an `Idempotency-Key` built from the order id and the attempt number. If a request times out and is sent again, the gateway returns the first result instead of charging twice.
A new `PaymentAttempt` table records each try with its decline code. Support can see why an order is waiting, and the rollout numbers come from this table.

watch.text: `payment_state` is a Postgres enum. Adding a value needs its own migration, which cannot run inside a transaction. Ship it before the code.

ask: How long does the gateway remember an idempotency key?

chapters.title: Roll it out behind a flag
explain: Ship the enum migration first, then the idempotency key (safe on its own), then the retry worker behind `payment_retry_enabled`. Turn it on for 10% of orders for a week, then for all of them.
Watch the numbers below each day. A double charge at any time means turn the flag off and refund by hand.

verdict.summary: The change is contained in checkout and one new worker, but it charges cards without the customer present. The idempotency key and the state check before each retry are what keep it safe.
